company_name: Zoomlion Heavy Industry Science and Technology Co., Ltd.

inputs.share_count_basis: 8,521m = issued ordinary shares excluding unvested restricted A shares at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim report note 7(a); total issued 8,648.5m incl. 127m unvested restricted shares whose cost is charged through the SBC line). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed. The 543m potential H shares from the RMB6bn 0.7% convertible bond due 2031 are EXCLUDED: the CB is carried as debt (RMB5,924m inside loans and borrowings) and its conversion price of HKD10.02 is far above the current price, so counting it in both debt and the share count would double-charge it. The diluted weighted-average of 9,064m in the Metrics CSV includes those CB shares and must not be used as the divisor.
inputs.debt_composition: Loans and borrowings 36,858 (current 10,392 + non-current 26,466, incl. CB liability component 5,924) + lease liabilities 733 (current 254 + non-current 479) = 37,591. Cash and cash equivalents 15,769; pledged bank deposits 2,309 (110 + 2,199) are restricted and deliberately NOT counted as cash. Balance sheet at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim report).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated cash flow statement, equity-settled share-based payment expense add-back (Metrics CSV StockBasedComp, RMB millions). Equity-award cash taxes are nil (KPI EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year); no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure is published, so the single add-back is the SBC charge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow for repurchase of H shares RMB96m (FY2024 54m, FY2023 1,085m, FY2022 1,556m). Buybacks have shrunk to token size while SBC runs RMB300-900m/yr, so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is funding only partially; SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); H shares quoted in HKD on HKEX. CNY->HKD 1.1728 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-16T04:41Z. Parity check against the Shenzhen A-share (000157.SZ, CNY 5.94 at 2026-10-16T04:26Z): 5.94 x 1.1728 = HKD 6.97 versus the observed H-share print, i.e. the H share trades at a ~23% discount to the A share, a normal A/H gap for a mainland industrial; the direction and magnitude of the rate are therefore confirmed. All per-share values are computed in CNY and converted at this rate; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value/weighted_iv are in HKD to match current_price.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T03:59:56Z (HKEX mid-session print, 11:59 HKT; regular-session intraday, not after-hours; refresh at the next close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: China 10-year CGB ~1.8%. Equity risk premium 8.0% (mature-market 5.5% plus a China/H-share country-and-governance premium of ~2.5%), beta 1.15 for a construction-machinery cyclical -> cost of equity ~11.0%. Cost of debt: FY2025 interest on borrowings RMB711m on ~RMB30bn average borrowings = 2.4% pre-tax, ~2.0% after tax (the RMB6bn CB carries a 0.7% coupon). Target capital structure 65/35 equity/debt by through-cycle market value (the current ~50% debt weight is inflated by borrowings that fund the customer-financing receivables book and by a depressed H-share price) -> 0.65 x 11.0 + 0.35 x 2.0 = 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, receivables credit risk and FX are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: IFRS 16 lease liabilities of RMB733m at 30 June 2026 are included in total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows and no lease_cost_pct_path is used; right-of-use depreciation remains inside the D&A path (D&A ex-ROU is not separately disclosed at the interim, and the lease book is ~2% of debt, so the tax effect is immaterial). Ongoing lease-asset renewal is implicitly inside the capex path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: flows are consolidated (EBITDA includes the ~3% of profit attributable to non-controlling interests), and the NCI balance of RMB2,166m at 30 June 2026 is deducted in equity_bridge. Calibration: FY2025 modelled NOPAT at a 13.0% owner-EBITDA margin (6,774 - 343 SBC - 1,528 D&A = 4,903 EBIT x 0.84 = ~4,120) sits below reported attributable net income of 4,779, the gap being the 13% book tax rate, +114 associates and the ~430m of non-recurring disposal gains deliberately excluded from the margin anchor.
inputs.excluded_income_and_matching_assets: Interest income (RMB469m FY2025) is stripped from owner FCF because cash is netted in the bridge. Share of profits of associates (114m) sits below profit from operations and is therefore outside EBITDA, so interests in associates (2,977m) are added in the bridge. Wealth-management products, securities funds and FVOCI equity securities (FVPL 2,555m + other financial assets 1,911m) are added at carrying/fair value; their FY2025 income (53m FV gains + 26m dividends) is inside other net income, but the margin anchor at 13.0% versus the 14.1% reported already excludes ~430m of non-recurring other-income items, far more than this ~80m, so the matching rule is satisfied conservatively. Pledged deposits (2,309m) are left out of both cash and the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon (margins still ramping at year 5), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with owner-fcf-adaptations.md applied (CNY/HKD currency split, leases as debt, NCI in bridge, matching assets, risk charged once). Not an SOE special case: Hunan SASAC is the largest holder at ~17.7% but the company is an ordinary consolidated manufacturer with a customer-financing book; the financing receivables are treated as operating working capital, not as a separate lender to be valued on book. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue 52,107, +14.6%). CYCLE POSITION: FY2025 is mid-cycle, not peak: domestic revenue (~43% of sales) is still far below the FY2020-21 peak while overseas (57% of H1 FY2026 revenue) is in a structural ramp; the reported EBITDA margin of 14.1% sits in the upper half of the 10-year 7.8-14.7% range, so the base anchors at 13.0% (reported less the 156m associate-disposal gain and ~half of the 548m recurring-but-lumpy PP&E disposal gains; government grants of 908m are treated as recurring operating subsidies, as they have been every year). OWNER FCF: negative in every year FY2021-FY2025 (reported FCF - SBC - interest income: -2,123, -737, -801, -4,081, -894; cumulative ~-8.6bn), because receivables and inventory have absorbed cash in up- and down-years alike while capex ran at ~9% of revenue in FY2024-25; the forward build therefore relies on capex tapering (H1 FY2026 capex 1,111 vs 2,603) and a working-capital capture of -35% of revenue growth, which is still a heavy drag. The RMB823m H1 FY2026 FX loss sits below EBITDA and is not in the margin. The Analysis JSON existed but was not valid JSON when read (another agent mid-write); its bull/bear and risk text was read verbatim and used for the scenario axes. Price is an intraday print and will be refreshed by the orchestrator.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim note 14, 30 June 2026; spare-cash investments whose income is outside the margin anchor

equity_bridge.item: Other financial assets (FVOCI strategic equity securities 1,595; FVPL listed/PE 216; term deposit 100)
Interests in associates at carrying value

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (4.3%) as the primary anchor, lifted to ~5% blended over the 10-year base path for the overseas mix shift; revenue and EPS 5-year CAGRs are negative only because FY2020 was the domestic cycle peak (revenue 65.1bn vs 52.1bn FY2025)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR +4.3% diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (-4.4%) and EPS (-10.7%) 5yr CAGRs, and the 3yr figures (+7.8% / +25.7%) point the other way: FY2020 was the domestic cycle peak and FY2022 the trough. Both windows are cycle artefacts; the base case is anchored on mid-cycle margins and a decelerating growth path rather than on either CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) was positive FY2018-FY2020 (3.6-4.9bn) and negative in every year FY2021-FY2025. Reported FCF went from +6,131 (FY2020) to -82 (FY2025). SBC (343m, 0.66% of revenue in FY2025; 866m in FY2024) is small relative to the swings, so the gap between reported and owner FCF is driven by interest income on the cash pile and by the working-capital build, not by stock comp.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at +8% follows H1 +9.2% (overseas +12.5%, domestic +5%) with a softer H2 as FX and tariff friction bite; decelerates to 2.5% as overseas penetration matures and domestic stays infrastructure-led rather than property-led.
base.margin_rationale: Anchor 13.0% = FY2025 reported 14.1% less non-recurring disposal gains; H1 FY2026 ex the 645m associate-disposal gain ran ~12.9%. Ramps 1pp over six years as higher-margin overseas and mining/aerial mix grows and the 10-year 7.8-14.7% range is respected at the terminal 14.0%.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex ran 8.9% of revenue in FY2024-25 (overseas plants in Hungary/Mexico/Brazil/Turkey, intelligent factories); H1 FY2026 capex of 1,111 (4.1%) shows the programme tapering. Path 5.0% -> 3.5%, converging just above D&A at 3.3% (D&A rises from 2.9% as the new plants depreciate).
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash tax paid 919 on PBT 5,794 = 15.9%; book rate 13.2% (HNTE 15% rate, R&D super-deduction 504m, lower-rate subsidiaries 341m). Ramps to 18% as overseas profit (taxed at local rates) grows and super-deductions dilute; statutory PRC rate is 25%.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables + contract assets are ~90% of revenue and grew ~10bn in FY2025 on a 6.6bn revenue increase; FY2025 OCF 4,573 vs NI + D&A ~6,555 implies ~2bn of WC drag (-30% of the revenue change), FY2023 -53%. -35% of the revenue change is the mid-cycle rate; negative because this is a manufacturer with receivables + inventory far exceeding payables.

bull.rationale: Domestic excavator cycle recovery (2026 industry data +17-25%) coincides with the overseas ramp; margin reaches 15.5%, the FY2020 peak level, on mix; the September 2026 US$300m credit-insurance and US$50m non-recourse factoring facilities plus tighter overseas credit terms cut the WC drag to -25% of growth. Still below the 16-18% margins of Western peers.

bear.rationale: A 2027-28 downturn: domestic infrastructure spend stalls after the 15th Five-Year Plan start, and an overseas credit/tariff event (anti-dumping action in the EU/US, emerging-market receivable defaults) forces higher ECL and price cuts. Revenue falls ~15% over two years (FY2022 fell 38% from the peak); EBITDA margin troughs at 9.5% (FY2022 trough was 7.8% on a far smaller overseas base). WC capture is set at -10%, far lower in absolute terms than the base -35%, because the capture is linear in the revenue CHANGE: in the FY2027-28 decline years a base-like capture would book a working-capital release of ~2bn, and in FY2022 and FY2024 the receivables book did NOT release cash as revenue fell. -10% keeps that windfall small; the cost of the receivables that fail to convert is carried instead in the 9.5-10% margin trough via ECL. A side effect is that bear owner FCF in FY2026-27 exceeds the base (slower growth finances fewer customers), which is the bear thesis stated in cash terms, not an error. Terminal margin 11.5% = the 10-year average.

scenario_narratives.base: Zoomlion is mid-way through turning from a China-construction cyclical into a globally diversified machinery OEM: overseas is 57% of revenue and growing ~12%, domestic is recovering from an infrastructure-led, not property-led, base. Revenue compounds ~5% blended over ten years, the EBITDA margin drifts from 13% to 14% on mix, capex tapers from the FY2024-25 factory build-out to ~3.5% of revenue, and working capital keeps absorbing about a third of every yuan of revenue growth because the business wins overseas share by financing its customers. Owner FCF turns positive in FY2026 for the first time since FY2020 but stays thin (~3-7% of revenue), which is why the equity value sits well below the book value of RMB57.6bn: the balance sheet is largely receivables and inventory that the model does not treat as liquid.
scenario_narratives.bull: The domestic cycle turns up in earnest (excavator sales +17-25% through 2026, equipment-renewal subsidies, Yaxi hydropower-scale projects) at the same time as overseas mining, aerial-platform and agricultural machinery compound, lifting revenue growth to double digits for three years. Mix and scale take the EBITDA margin to 15.5%, the FY2020 peak. Credit insurance, non-recourse factoring and tighter overseas terms cut the WC drag, so the cash conversion that has been missing since FY2020 finally appears. The axes are the domestic cycle, overseas margin, and whether receivables stop eating the growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: H1 FY2026 already showed the cost of the growth model: profit fell 24% on +9% revenue (FX loss 823m, gross margin 26.8% vs 28.1%), debt is up 10bn in 18 months to 36.9bn, and receivables plus finance-lease and guarantee exposure (4.8bn of customer-financing guarantees) are the collateral. In the bear a domestic relapse and an overseas trade or credit event hit together in 2027-28, revenue falls 15%, ECL and price cuts take the margin to 9.5%, and, as in FY2022 and FY2024, the receivables book does not unwind to fund the gap. Governance (Hunan SASAC at 17.7%, connected transactions such as the RMB904m finance-leasing stake bought from the parent in 2025) is an overlay, not a separate scenario.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: owner FCF has been negative for five straight years, net debt has risen ~10bn in 18 months, receivables are ~90% of revenue with 4.8bn of off-balance-sheet customer-financing guarantees, and 57% of revenue is now exposed to tariff and emerging-market credit risk. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: a sustained domestic upcycle, overseas margin expansion, and working-capital discipline that the company has not yet demonstrated. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical manufacturer valued on the cash it can actually return to owners, not on the receivables-and-inventory book it reports as equity. Margins are anchored to a mid-cycle 13% rather than the FY2025 reported 14.1%, capex is allowed to taper only as far as the H1 FY2026 run-rate already shows, and working capital is charged against growth at the rate the last three years actually consumed it. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, at a single CNY-built WACC of 8%; the terminal multiple is capped at 13x FCF because no buyer has paid a compounder's multiple for a Chinese construction-machinery OEM through a full cycle. The equity bridge adds the financial-asset and associate stakes whose income is outside EBITDA and deducts minorities once. Values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD at a dated rate with an A-share parity check.
key_risks_to_valuation: Working-capital capture (-35% of revenue growth in base) is the single most sensitive driver: at the FY2023 rate of -53% owner FCF roughly halves; at the bull -25% it rises by a third.
Terminal cap at 13x FCF binds in base and bull (Gordon at 8%/2.5% implies ~18.6x); relaxing the cap toward the Gordon value adds materially to IV and is the re-rating bet, not the house view.

Receivables credit: 47bn of trade receivables and contract assets plus 6.1bn finance-lease receivables and 4.8bn of guarantees; ECL is inside the margin, but a systemic default wave in an export market is in no scenario's flows beyond the bear margin trough.
FX: RMB appreciation against USD/EUR/BRL produced an 823m H1 FY2026 loss; translation and transaction effects are excluded from EBITDA and not modelled.
Capex re-acceleration: management's embodied-robotics and hydrogen programmes could keep capex at the 9% FY2024-25 rate rather than tapering to 3.5%.

Convertible bond: treated as debt at 5.9bn; if the H share rallied above HKD10.02 and holders converted, debt falls by ~6bn but the count rises 543m (~6%); the two roughly offset at that price and the valuation is insensitive to the treatment below it.

Share-count basis: 8,521m excludes 127m unvested restricted A shares paid for via SBC and the CB shares; using the 9,064m diluted figure in the CSV would understate per-share value by ~6% while still carrying the CB in debt.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for 1157.HK at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HKD 5.18-10.67. A-share parity via 000157.SZ and CNYHKD=X from the same API (see inputs.fx_note).
data_sources.financials: 1157.HK_Metrics.csv (financial-parser agent, RMB millions, FY2018-H1 FY2026) and the H1 FY2026 interim report for all 30 June 2026 balance-sheet anchors (loans and borrowings note 16, lease liabilities, cash note 15, FVPL note 14, other financial assets note 10, interests in associates, NCI, EPS note 7, guarantees note 21); FY2025 annual report for the income statement, other net income note 4, tax reconciliation note 6(b) and business outlook.
data_sources.qualitative: 1157.HK_Analysis.json (qualitative-analyst agent; the file was not valid JSON at read time, so its bull_case, bear_case and risks text was read directly) plus the H1 FY2026 MD&A for segment and geographic revenue and management's outlook.
